READING

**Constructing the TREVANNOCK net per season**

Vantwyn pays £168 × 400 = £67,200.

Against that I charge three costs.

*Lost borage.* Those 400 colonies come out of the orchards too late for Kirkhallow. Borage returned £71 a colony last season, so the lost margin is 400 × £71 = £28,400.

*Spray losses.* Whinnerdale lost 9 % of placed colonies. Nine per cent of 400 is 36 colonies, each costing £210 to replace: 36 × £210 = £7,560. This is a cash cost paid to restore the working fleet; it does not include any productivity drag while a new split builds up.

*Haulage and labour.* £6,900.

Net per season: £67,200 − £28,400 − £7,560 − £6,900 = **£24,340**.

Over three seasons (2027, 2028, 2029): **£73,020**.

---

**Equipment proceeds: the pivot of the comparison**

Under ORMSCLEUCH, Ravensgate pays £96,000 now (before the 28 November 2026 close).

Under TREVANNOCK, the kit is used through the end of the 2029 season. The lorry then loses its vale permit on 1 January 2030. The problem states the whole kit is worth about £20,000 at that point.

Equipment advantage of ORMSCLEUCH: £96,000 − £20,000 = **£76,000**.

---

**The arithmetic balance**

| | £ |
|---|---|
| TREVANNOCK three-year operational surplus | +73,020 |
| ORMSCLEUCH equipment advantage | −76,000 |
| **Net in simple arithmetic (ORMSCLEUCH ahead)** | **−2,980** |

In undiscounted terms ORMSCLEUCH wins by under £3,000. That margin looks razor-thin, but it moves in only one direction once real-world factors are applied.

---

**Time value**

The £96,000 lands in hand at the end of 2026. The £73,020 operational surplus is spread across three future seasons and the £20,000 residual arrives at the end of 2029 — roughly three years hence. Even at a modest 5 % discount rate the present value of TREVANNOCK's future cash flows is closer to £83,000 in total, widening ORMSCLEUCH's lead to roughly £13,000. At any higher rate the gap grows further. Time value alone turns a statistical tie into a clear margin.

---

**Spray-loss risk is one-sided**

The 9 % figure comes from one grower, one season. Vantwyn will not vary their spray programme, which is the same inflexibility that cost Whinnerdale 9 %. If Thistledown's losses ran to 15 % (60 colonies), replacement cost rises to £12,600 and the annual net falls from £24,340 to about £19,300; over three seasons the operational surplus drops from £73,020 to £57,900 and ORMSCLEUCH's advantage more than doubles. The spray risk can only hurt TREVANNOCK; it cannot help it.

---

**What happens after 2029 under TREVANNOCK?**

The Vantwyn contract runs three years and then stops. The lorry has no vale permit from 2030. The kit is worth £20,000 — not enough to describe as a platform for anything. Thistledown would need fresh pollination contracts with a severely impaired haulage asset and a track record of the original three contracts (the ones that justified the £187,000 outlay) all failing to renew. TREVANNOCK does not preserve a viable migratory business beyond 2029; it defers exit by three years and extracts marginally less money for the kit in the process.

---

**Coldharbour and Nyefield**

Two vale growers have asked for a rate for 2028. No contract has been tendered, no terms offered. The original three contracts that funded the kit were all considered sound enough to invest against, and none renewed. The track record of this business converting enquiries into durable revenue is poor. Weighting unconfirmed interest against a confirmed £96,000 offer in hand is not supported by the evidence.

---

**Summary table (undiscounted, three-year horizon)**

| | TREVANNOCK | ORMSCLEUCH |
|---|---|---|
| Vantwyn receipts | £201,600 | — |
| Lost borage (400 × £71 × 3) | (£85,200) | — |
| Spray replacements | (£22,680) | — |
| Haulage | (£20,700) | — |
| Equipment proceeds | £20,000 (end 2029) | £96,000 (now) |
| **Net** | **£93,020** | **£96,000** |

Time value, one-sided spray risk, and the absence of any credible migratory pipeline after 2029 all reinforce what the raw figures already suggest.

---

CALL
  ORMSCLEUCH

GROUNDS
  Selling the kit to Ravensgate for £96,000 now beats TREVANNOCK's three-year operational surplus of £73,020 even before discounting, and once time value and the one-sided spray-loss risk are included the case for ORMSCLEUCH is unambiguous.
